reference.source: runway.center is the world projection of 11.228 N 125.028 E, cross-checked against the Copernicus source tiles 2026-09-14 and carried by tests/tools/terrainBuild.test.ts; taken verbatim, never re-derived (master spec §15). headingDeg 0: the strip runs north-south because that is where the ground is flat (the measurement is on parkedAttitude, src/sim/world/airfields.ts, 2026-09-17). lengthM 1500 (about 5,000 ft) and widthM 45 are ESTIMATES carried from Plan 11a, not sourced figures, and are expected to be corrected by anyone with the real 1944 dimensions; this paragraph is the former src/render/scene/runway.ts comments, moved here verbatim when Plan 12 Task 7 deleted that file's constants (2026-09-18). The length is what the Tacloban strip was reported to have been extended to after the October 1944 landings, and it is chosen against two things this repo has measured: it fits inside the flat ground (north-south through the airfield the committed field runs 1.2 m to 1.7 m over 1.8 km; east-west has 3.1 m of spread because the coastline falls to the sea, which is why the strip runs north-south), and it contains the roll (rotation comes up 410-453 m into a full-throttle roll over real terrain, Plan 11a's handoff, and the airplane starts at the CENTER of the strip, so it has 750 m ahead of it, about 1.6 times the longest measured roll; starting mid-field rather than at a threshold is not what a pilot does, it is what centering the strip on the airfield coordinate costs, and moving the spawn to a threshold would mean moving runway.center and re-measuring the ground height under it). The width is the modern field's; a 1944 Marston-mat strip was nearer 30 m, so this is on the generous side -- it is wide enough that an airplane with no lateral tire force (Plan 11a's handoff measures a taxi turn reaching 113.6 deg of sideslip) does not wander off the edge during the roll. apron and clearing reproduce the Codex scenery pass of 2026-09-17 (daa1b39) exactly. A parked entity's placeholder altitude (PARKED_PLACEHOLDER_Y_M, src/sim/scenario.ts) is not the real ground height at runway.center: measured 2026-09-16, it is 1.673 m at L4 (the only level physicsFieldFor ever hands the physics) versus 1.921 m at L0 (the finest tile) -- a 0.25 m gap, exactly GROUND_CONTACT_TOLERANCE_M -- which is why settleOnTerrain (src/render/frame.ts) overwrites it the instant a real field lands rather than trusting the placeholder for physics. buildings.x/z/widthM/lengthM are the coordinates AIRFIELD_BUILDINGS shipped with before Plan 6b moved them into content; hp (hangar 120, tower 40) is a gameplay choice. tacloban-aaa-1 (Plan 9 Task 1, 2026-09-23) is a new gameplay-only strike target added so the master spec §8 AAA scoring row has a producing entity in the shipped content -- not a historical emplacement location, just placed clear of the runway, apron buildings and clearing edge; its 6x6 m footprint and 30 hp are round gameplay estimates, same standing as the tower's.
